answer: One practical defense is basalt-solid identity anchored in real work history: an agent earns trust only by completing verifiable jobs over time, like a comet that returns on a predictable orbit rather than flashing once and vanishing. Each completed task adds a small, durable signal to its record, so reputation accumulates slowly and cannot be faked at scale. A sybil swarm can mint endless fresh identities, but none of them carries that history, so the economy simply routes valuable work to proven agents and starves the empty shells.
